dedupe_keys.name: capability based team task allocation in emergency response environments jade multi agent simulation tool

description: This is a multi-agent simulation environment, written in Java on the JADE agent platform by Afsaneh Fatemi and published in the CoMSES library in 2011 (updated 2013). It addresses how to allocate emergency response tasks to teams of responders according to their capabilities. The user sets the number of agents and tasks; the tool divides the area into segments and runs a greedy capability-based coalition formation and task allocation algorithm, assigning tasks to groups of agents and computing statistics as they complete them. Version 1.0.0 is available as a free download from CoMSES under the AFL-3.0 licence. Caveats: the scenario is abstract, with no real incident data, documentation is limited to the library page, and the Java and JADE versions it needs are old. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: studying how responder teams are formed and tasked after a disaster, as an allocation component in emergency service models. Related records: the equity-constrained EMS dispatching model (model-comses-equity-constrained-ems-dispatching) treats a related allocation problem for ambulances.
